meta.title: The Census Taker's Round
meta.skill_frame: Work out what a word means from the passage: use the sentence around it, not a dictionary guess.

reader.who: Students who read at about a fourth-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Measured FK 6.8, 6.7, 5.3 (6.2 together) on the 3 parts. The load is an institution with its own vocabulary and a claim that reverses the reader's expectation: one form is worthless and thousands are valuable.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.text_status: Drafted for the band, review pending.
source.survey: The census round as work, so 'household' and 'return' are learned from what the taker did with them.
source.avoided: No country, year, or office is named. No invented population numbers.

session.difficulty_basis: Clue distance: the term is defined by the form and the round, not by a glossary.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: Once every ten years, a census taker walked a district and knocked on every door. The census is a count of people. The count decides how many representatives a place gets, and how much money it receives. The taker carried a form with a column for each fact: name, age, occupation, and place of birth. It also asked how each person was related to the head of the household. A household is everyone living under one roof, whether or not they are related. The taker wrote what he was told, and he was not allowed to guess. A guess would make one house different from the next.
passage.part_2: The work was slow and often unwelcome. A taker returned to a house three times before he could record it as empty. A missed house is a missed person, and it cannot be corrected later. Some families gave ages that did not fit the children standing beside them. The taker recorded the answer anyway. A return is the sheet a taker filed. Its value depends on every entry being treated the same way, even the doubtful ones. One careful taker and one careless one would otherwise produce two different countries. The rules were long for that reason. A taker who invented his own answers was not kept.
passage.part_3: The census is read long after the knock. A historian can compare one decade with the next. A street may change from workshops to apartments. A family may shrink as children leave. No single form says any of this. The pattern appears only when thousands of returns are stacked together. That is the strange power of the count. It tells nothing important about one house and something important about all of them. A street that looks the same in two photographs may hold different people, and the forms show it. Nothing in one return is interesting. The interest is in the difference between one return and the next.

items.prompt:
A ____ is everyone living under one roof, whether or not they are related.

Write the missing word.

tutor_only.confirm: Right. Everyone under one roof is a household.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The first part defines a household as everyone living under one roof, related or not.
tutor_only.tell: The word is household. It counts people by roof, not by family name.
help: Look at the fifth sentence of the passage.
The word is defined right there.

if_they_say.ask: Family is not the test. What is the test?

tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case and punctuation. Accept household or house hold.

items.prompt: What is a return in this passage?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. A return is the filed sheet for one household.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The second part says a return is the sheet a taker filed.
tutor_only.tell: A return is the completed sheet the taker filed for one household.
help: Look at the sentence beginning 'A return is'.
It names what the taker filed.

if_they_say.when: the student says it is when the taker comes back
if_they_say.ask: Coming back is 'returned to a house'. What is the sheet called?

if_they_say.when: the student says it is the whole census
if_they_say.ask: The whole census is thousands of them. What is one sheet?

tutor_only.core_idea: The sheet a census taker filled in and filed for a household.
accept_ideas: the completed sheet for one house
the record the taker handed in

items.prompt:
A taker returned to a house three times before he could ____ it as empty.

Write the missing word.

tutor_only.confirm: Right. He recorded the house as empty.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The second part says a taker returned three times before he could record it as empty.
tutor_only.tell: The word is record. It means writing the result on the form.
help: Look at the second sentence of the part above.

if_they_say.ask: Marking is close. What word does the passage use for writing it on the form?

tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case and punctuation. Accept record, including a clear misspelling such as recrd.

items.prompt: Why did the taker record ages he doubted?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. He wrote what he was told, because guessing would break the rule.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The first part says he was not allowed to guess; the second says every entry was treated the same way, even doubtful ones.
tutor_only.tell: The taker wrote the answer as given. A count where each taker guesses is worth less than one where all follow the same rule.
help: Look at the last sentence of the earlier part.
Then read the last sentence of the part above.

if_they_say.when: the student says he believed the family
if_they_say.ask: Belief is not the point. What was he not allowed to do?

if_they_say.when: the student says he had no time to check
if_they_say.ask: Time is not the reason given. What rule governed every entry?

tutor_only.core_idea: Because every entry had to be treated the same way, so a doubtful answer was written as given rather than guessed at.
accept_ideas: he was not allowed to guess
the rule was to write what he was told
consistency mattered more than correcting the family
not_required: who the head of the household was

items.prompt: The passage says the count tells nothing important about one house and something important about all of them. What does that mean?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The information lives in the whole set, not in one sheet.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The last part says no single form shows the change, and the pattern appears only when thousands of returns are stacked together.
tutor_only.tell: One form is a single case. The meaning appears only when thousands are compared with each other.
help: Look at the last two sentences of the passage.
The second one explains the first.

if_they_say.when: the student says one house is not important to the taker
if_they_say.ask: The phrase is about what the count can show. Where does the pattern appear?

if_they_say.when: the student says all houses are the same
if_they_say.ask: The passage says a street can change from workshops to apartments. What makes that visible?

tutor_only.core_idea: A single form shows little, but thousands together reveal patterns like a street changing or families shrinking.
accept_ideas: one form says little, but many forms show patterns
the value comes from comparing thousands of returns
a single house is not interesting, but the whole set is
